Quick triage notes (initial):
- Reproduced decode stalls in traces: stalls appear on warm KV-cache hits with the q2-int8 kernels when sequences > 512 tokens. Small inputs are fine.
- Root cause hypothesis: the q2-int8 execution path has a suboptimal tensor-layout kernel that serializes a portion of the attention/multistep decode under high concurrency; this amplifies tail latency and causes occasional request timeouts which return 500.
- Affected subset: dedicated pool nodes with driver build r54 and kernel set k-q2-int8-202705. Hosted and non-quant variants unaffected.

Immediate mitigations we can do now:
1) Route Spectro traffic to the v5-fp16 variant (no quant) — this removes quant kernels and should restore latency to baseline within 5–10 minutes.
2) Disable Q-cache for this dedicated pool to avoid the warm-hit path until we patch the kernel (minor TPU-like perf loss).
3) Rollback quant profile on the dedicated pool to previous profile q1 (safe, known).

I'll open INF-8421 to track the kernel/compat fix and a regression test; link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8421. Attaching a small trace extract (trace_dump_20270525.txt).

Planned timeline if approved now:
- 16:50 PT: switch routing to v5-fp16 (quick, no restart).
- 17:30 PT: rollback quant profile on dedicated nodes (requires short rolling-restart per node, estimated 8–12 minutes of degraded capacity).
- 20:00 PT: test patch candidate in canary and re-enable q-cache once fixed.

I'll standby for Ben/Monica to confirm customer communication window.

— Rishi
